In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the problem of satisfiability of 3CNF formula above the threshold is in the class of #P.
the complexity of solving satisfiable random 3-SAT formulas above the threshold depends on the distribution of the formulas, and is not necessarily the same for all distributions.
the problem of finding satisfying assignments to 3-SAT formulas above the threshold is solvable in low exponential time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we give the first polynomial time algorithm for finding satisfying assignments for random formulas above the threshold, and the first algorithm for finding satisfying assignment in time sub-exponential in the size of the formula.
we have shown that the “phase transition” in random 3-SAT is algorithmic.

for a random formula of n variables and m clauses, with probability 1, the formula can be solved in time 2^{O(m^{1.5})}, if m > n log^{3/4}(n), and the formula can be found to be unsatisfiable in time 2^O(n), if m > n^{2/3} log^2(n).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the complexity of solving 3-SAT above the threshold is significantly less than the general case, where the problem is believed to be intractable.
the complexity of finding satisfying assignments of 3-SAT formulas depends on the complexity of the formula, not on the complexity of its satisfying assignment.
the satisfiability problem above the threshold can be solved by algorithms that are significantly more efficient than the ones known for the general 3-SAT problem.
